narrative.overview: This is the look of a trek operator who has run the logistics a thousand times and wants you to feel that before you've even picked a route: a dark, factual strip up top stating the government registration number next to the reassurance ("your exciting Himalaya experience is in safe hands"), a calm glacier-teal identity running through links, chrome, and primary actions, and a single flag-orange used only where something needs a traveler's eyes — an icon, an active menu item, a price tag. Nothing about this system performs; it reports. Cards are flat rectangles with a whisper of shadow, not stacked paper or glossy tiles. Headings are set in a clean condensed sans at regular weight — never bold, never shouting — because the confidence here comes from specificity (altitude figures, duration, government reg. numbers, WhatsApp numbers with a real first name attached) rather than from typographic volume. It is not a glossy destination-marketing site chasing emotion through full-bleed imagery; imagery supports the briefing, it doesn't replace it. The system was never designed to feel minimal for its own sake — it inherited a bootstrap-era pragmatism (Bootstrap 4 grid, Owl Carousel, SmartMenus) — but that pragmatism is the point: it reads as operationally credible rather than as a template.
keyCharacteristics: Calm, cool, glacier-blue identity color rather than an "adventure" red/orange-dominant palette
A single accent (signal orange) spent sparingly on icons and active states — never on large surfaces
Flat, sharp-cornered cards and bars; roundness is reserved for pill/CTA buttons and circular controls
Regular-weight (not bold) Montserrat headings paired with Poppins body text
A persistent top strip carrying government registration and a trust tagline — credibility stated as fact, not as a badge graphic

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange never fills a background larger than an icon or a button; its job is to mark the thing worth noticing, not to decorate.

rules.name: The Teal-Never-Loud Rule
rules.body: Teal is the identity color precisely because it stays calm — it is never paired with saturated warm colors at equal weight, which is why orange is rationed instead of balanced against it.

rules.name: The No-Bold-Headings Rule
rules.body: Headings never go above weight 400. Hierarchy is built with size and the eyebrow label, not boldness.

rules.name: The Whisper-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a shadow is added, it stays at or below rgba(0,0,0,0.08). A card that announces its elevation is off-system.

rules.name: The Content-Stays-Sharp Rule
rules.body: Anything that holds information (cards, bands, menus) is square-cornered. Roundness is earned only by things you click to act.

dos: Do keep orange confined to icons, active states, and at most one CTA per view — it is a pointer, not a fill color.
Do keep headings at Montserrat weight 400; build emphasis with size and the uppercase eyebrow label instead of bold.
Do pair sharp-cornered content surfaces with pill or circular interactive controls — don't round a card to match a button.
Do keep card elevation at or below the Card Ambient shadow value; let the hairline border and background contrast do most of the separation work.

Do carry the top utility strip's factual tone (registration numbers, direct phone lines with a first name) into any new trust-building surface — specificity is this brand's credibility mechanism, not badges or stock imagery.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent color alongside Signal Orange — the system's calm comes from having exactly one "loud" color.
Don't give structural surfaces (cards, bands, menus) rounded corners; that roundness vocabulary is reserved for buttons and circular controls.
Don't bold headings or increase their weight for emphasis.
Don't add drop shadows beyond the whisper-level Card Ambient value — nothing in this system should look like it's floating.
